name: Oklo
description: Oklo is a pre-revenue developer of small fast-neutron nuclear reactors it calls Aurora powerhouses (15 MWe to 75 MWe and larger designs). Its plan is to build, own and operate the plants and sell electricity and heat directly to customers under long-term power purchase agreements, rather than sell reactor designs to utilities. It also owns Atomic Alchemy (bought February 28, 2025), a radioisotope producer, and is working on nuclear fuel fabrication and recycling. It has almost no revenue (1.2 million dollars in Q2 2026, its first) and a net loss of 81.6 million dollars in the first half of 2026, but a large cash pile of 3.0 billion dollars at June 30, 2026 raised by selling shares (an at-the-market program of up to 1.5 billion dollars was set up in December 2025). Nothing is generating power yet: the first powerhouse at Idaho National Laboratory is targeted for 2028, subject to Nuclear Regulatory Commission and Department of Energy approvals. The main value drivers are regulatory milestones, customer deals such as Meta's prepayment for a 1.2 GW Ohio campus, and fuel supply.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. SEC SIC code 4911 (Electric Services). Oklo has no power plant operating yet and earns almost nothing, so the utility label describes the plan, not the business today.

hq.note: City and state from the EDGAR submissions record

employees.note: 205 full-time employees in 33 US states plus 2 in Canada; FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: Aurora powerhouses (power and heat sales)
businessLines.how: Plans to sell electricity and heat under long-term power purchase agreements while owning and operating the plants; no power sold yet. Meta's January 5, 2026 prepayment agreement lets Meta prepay for power, and Oklo uses the money to buy nuclear fuel for the first phase.
businessLines.description: Small fast-reactor plants designed to run on fresh, recycled or down-blended fuel; first plant (Aurora-INL) planned at Idaho National Laboratory, with a 1.2 GW campus planned in Pike County, Ohio for Meta and a tentative selection to serve Eielson Air Force Base, Alaska. Kiewit Nuclear Solutions is lead constructor for the first plant.

businessLines.name: Radioisotopes (Atomic Alchemy)
businessLines.how: Sells isotopes per batch or contract to customers; first revenue of 1.2 million dollars in Q2 2026 (the two prior comparison periods show none).
businessLines.description: Produces radioisotopes for medical, energy, industry, defense and AI uses; two projects (Oklo) and one (Atomic Alchemy) were selected by DOE in August 2025 for its reactor pilot program; a DOE agreement for a radioisotope pilot plant was signed January 7, 2026.

businessLines.name: Fuel fabrication and recycling
businessLines.how: Cost centre today: it secures fuel (including HALEU, high-assay low-enriched uranium, whose cost has risen sharply) for its own plants; recycling is intended to lower fuel cost and could later serve others.
businessLines.description: Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility at INL for the first powerhouse's fuel and development of nuclear fuel recycling; DOE has approved its Safety Design Strategy and conceptual design report.

brands.name: Aurora-INL (Idaho National Laboratory)
brands.share: First planned commercial-scale powerhouse; targeted 2028 deployment; site use permit granted by DOE

brands.name: Pike County, Ohio campus
brands.share: Planned 1.2 GW; land bought December 2025; supported by Meta prepayment agreement

brands.name: Atomic Alchemy
brands.share: Sole source of reported revenue (1.2 million dollars in Q2 2026)

Custom combined license application to the NRC; Phase I pre-application readiness assessment completed July 2025
